items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: Goddard Lieberson who was president of Columbia Records was a graduate of Juilliard.

ctx.x: Great. Well I wish you a lot of success with it and I am fascinated by your combination over the years of business sense, with the great musicianship. That’s rare. I think that’s rare. Because I’ve talked to a number of people who bemoan the fact that the people in power in the music world these days seem to have no musical sense or whatever. And so it’s nice to see it.

Well there has been quite a change. When I started I mentioned Mitch Miller who was an oboe player, and Goddard Lieberson who was president of Columbia Records was a graduate of Juilliard. And they were musicians, or if they weren’t musicians they were guys that wished they could have been musicians that were in [coughs] they were musicians or guys that at least wished they could have been musicians. Now in the record companies they are more concentrating on what’s at the bottom line, how much money did we make…

Beat and Record World and Variety and those magazines, Billboard. They really gave me a lot of space. Of course in the final analysis I had owe a lot to the people that I hit that heart string and recorded that song they fell in love to, and they went out and bought the albums. I have to thank all them too. They’ve been great and they’ve stayed with me for years.
